wave: Phase B final wave -- cache + washington (2026-08-23)
method: pdftoppm full-page render + Read tool (Claude Code allotment; no Anthropic API)

contributions.detail: GENERATION-1 Carr Printing 5-5-PG form: Form A prints NO schedule total at all (the sheet ends with '(If additional space is needed, use blank paper ...)'), so schedule_total is null and the cover's line 1 is the ONLY anchor - stated rather than invented. The 5 itemized rows sum to exactly 2,650.00, which equals BOTH the THIS REPORT cell and the CUMULATIVE cell (2,650 in each). The LAST REPORT cell is blank, so this is the filer's first report of the cycle and the two scopes coincide - recorded 'cumulative' with the coincidence stated. Line 2 (the $50-or-less aggregate) is blank in all three columns and anchors nothing. The 2,650.00 row sum is independently confirmed by the balance chain, which closes to the cent (see balance_chain) - that second, cents-bearing equation is what settles two bistable cent groups on this filing.

expenditures.detail: Form B also prints NO schedule total (Generation-1 form), so the cover's line 3 is the only anchor. The 12 itemized rows sum to exactly 6,333.06 = the THIS REPORT cell = the CUMULATIVE cell; the LAST REPORT cell is blank, so the scopes coincide on the first report of the cycle. Two individual figures were REVERSED by this arithmetic rather than by any glyph re-read - see escalation_note and the row notes for lines 2 and 11.

gates.page_subtotal: NO PRINTED SCHEDULE TOTAL EXISTS ON EITHER SHEET (Generation-1 form) - said plainly rather than invented. Gated against the cover instead, and every gate closes to the cent: p2 5 rows = 2,650.00 = cover line 1 (THIS and CUMULATIVE); p3 12 rows = 6,333.06 = cover line 3 (THIS and CUMULATIVE); and 2,650.00 - 6,333.06 = -3,683.06 = cover line 4 (THIS and CUMULATIVE). Three independent equations, all exact.
gates.row_count: rowbands.py reports geometry_status 'gaps' on both sheets and finds NO vertical rules at all - expected, because the Generation-1 form is an UNDERLINE form (writing lines, not a boxed grid), so the tool's grid model does not apply here. Its horizontal ladder is nevertheless regular at a 2.29-pct pitch on p3 and ~2.28 on p2 once the rules hidden under ink are interpolated, and I mapped the bands on the page by hand from it. Ink counted by eye at 200 dpi (normalized) and confirmed against the ladder: p2 5 inked lines then empty to the footer note; p3 12 inked lines then empty to the footer note. 5 and 12 rows emitted.
gates.geometry_proof: p2: first-row box pct:81.90,8.50,10.00,2.45@p2 renders '1,000.oo'; last-row box pct:81.90,17.75,10.00,2.20@p2 renders '100.00'; the control one pitch below (y=19.95) renders EMPTY. p3: first-row box pct:82.20,7.90,11.00,2.29@p3 renders '$425.0'; last-row box pct:82.20,33.08,11.00,2.25@p3 renders '980.00'; the control one pitch below (y=35.37) renders EMPTY. Row indices unshifted on both sheets.
gates.balance_chain: CLOSES EXACTLY AND IS THE DECISIVE GATE ON THIS FILING. Cover line 4 is written '- 3,683.06' in both the THIS and CUMULATIVE columns (a leading minus - the campaign is in deficit, which the accounting convention makes a negative balance, not an error). 0 beginning + 2,650.00 contributions - 6,333.06 expenditures = -3,683.06 exactly. Because that equation carries CENTS while cover line 1 is written without them ('2,650'), it is the check that pins the contributions side to 2,650.00 and no other value, and it is what settled the bistable cent group on Form A line 3. No earlier filing by this filer is in this chunk and every LAST-REPORT cell is blank, so the cross-filing TOTALS-FROM-LAST-REPORT chain has nothing to run against.

escalation_note: This is a faded photocopy of a Generation-1 form; every page was re-rendered with `magick -normalize` before reading and NINE cells were escalated. THREE VALUES WERE DECIDED BY ARITHMETIC AGAINST A HIGHER-RESOLUTION GLYPH READ (the Rhodes rule): (1) COVER LINE 1 CUMULATIVE read '3,650' on the 90-dpi contact sheet and '2,650' at 200 dpi normalized; a 600-dpi crop of the cell confirms 2, and the balance chain closes only under 2,650 - a textbook case of the brief's warning that the low-res sheet is never the source. (2) FORM B LINE 2 cents read '.65' at 900 and 1200 dpi, but the page's cents must sum to .06 (the three cent-bearing rows are the only source of cents in a 6,333.06 total) and only .68 + .69 + .69 = 2.06 delivers it; recorded .68. (3) FORM B LINE 11 read '152.00' at 200 dpi; the dollar sum was then exactly 5.00 short, and at 1200 dpi the third glyph is a flat-topped 7, giving 157.00 and closing the page to the cent. Also escalated: Form A line 3's amount (a doubled/overwritten superscript cent group that looks like '80' and is settled as .00 by two independent equations), Form A line 3's donor name (still not resolved - see the row note), Form B line 1's amount (a single slashed zero after the point), Form B line 2's date (still not resolved - left blank), Form B lines 9-12's dates (the leading '1' of '10' is a faint tick at the left margin), and the two geometry-proof triples.
notes: GENERATION 1 - the Carr Printing '5-5-PG' form, footer 'Carr Printing Company, Bountiful, Utah', cover citing Utah Code 17-16-6.5, three sheets plus (not present here) the statute page. Consequences respected throughout: NO in-kind column on either schedule (so in_kind is false on every row and no inference is made), NO printed schedule total on either schedule (so the cover is the only anchor), and ~40 underline writing lines rather than a boxed grid. FORM vs CHUNK FILE: the chunk file says candidate 'Greg Aldred', office 'Commission Seat C'; the cover's Full Name line reads 'Greg Aldred' and its 'Name of Office' line reads 'County Commissioner Seat C' - AGREES, county office, in scope. Office District is blank; Political Party is written 'Unaffiliated'. There is NO school-district line on this form generation. DATE DISCREPANCY WITH THE CHUNK FILE / FILE NAME: the file is named '...10_26_2016 FCR...', but the form is SIGNED '10-27-16' and the clerk's RECEIVED stamp reads OCT 27 2016 - the document says the 27th, the label says the 26th; the DOCUMENT governs. NOT the same filer as any other document in this chunk. PRIVACY: the cover prints the candidate's home street address, ZIP and home phone in the clear and Form A's address column holds street lines and a PO box - all discarded at read time; only donor city (and state where the filer wrote one, which he did not) is recorded. A separate note on Form A: three of the five donor rows carry NO address at all, so their donor_city is honestly blank, not withheld.

contributions.note: date written '3-1-16'. Donor written in block capitals 'SUHBA' with no expansion given on the form; the address cell is left entirely EMPTY by the filer, so donor_city/donor_state are honestly blank. Cents written as a superscript pair over the rule ('1,000.oo') - transcribed with a decimal point per the currency convention.
date written '3-9-16'. Address cell left EMPTY by the filer. Superscript cents over the rule.

date written '9-13-16'. DONOR NAME NOT RESOLVED: escalated to 1200 dpi with normalization and the first word remains a compressed cursive that reads 'Amedian' / 'Anedian' / possibly 'American'; the second reads 'Samuria' (possibly 'Samurai'); the third is clearly 'Builders'. Recorded as the legible glyph string at low confidence with needs_review rather than expanded to a plausible company name. AMOUNT: the cent group is a doubled/overwritten superscript that looks like '80' at 1200 dpi; settled as .00 by TWO independent equations - the five rows must sum to cover line 1 (2,650) and the balance chain must close at -3,683.06, and both hold only under 1,000.00. Address cell held a PO box and a city; the PO box was discarded at read time, leaving the city; the filer wrote no state.
date written '10-15-16'. Address cell held a street line and the city; the street line was discarded at read time. The filer wrote no state.
date written '10-24-16'. Address cell held a street line and the city; the street line was discarded at read time. The filer wrote no state.

expenditures.note: amount transcribed VERBATIM as '425.0' - the filer wrote a single slashed zero after the decimal point, not two; escalated to 1200 dpi and there is no second digit. The page arithmetic requires zero cents on this line, so the value is 425 dollars exactly; not silently padded to '425.00'.

DATE LEFT BLANK: verbatim the cell reads '2-/0?/16' - it carries a STRAY SLASH after the month and its day digit is an open 'c'-shaped glyph that is 5 or 6 even at 1200 dpi with normalization. Not cleanly parseable, so blank + needs_review with the verbatim kept here; no arithmetic can settle a date. AMOUNT: the cent group reads '.65' at 900 and 1200 dpi, but this page's cents can only come from lines 2, 3 and 4, and the printed total's .06 requires .68 + .69 + .69 = 2.06; recorded .68 on the arithmetic, with the glyph doubt recorded here. Vendor glyphs read 'Walmart'/'Welmart'.
same amount as line 3 - two distinct inked lines, confirmed in the 500 dpi band re-read and against the rule ladder. The vendor is written without the 'St. George' prefix here.
vendor written as two words here and 'Steam rollers' on line 11 - kept verbatim per line.
vendor written with an internal capital, 'CHerry Creek radio' - kept verbatim. The leading '1' of the month is written as a small tick at the left margin (see the note on lines 10-12).

on lines 10, 11 and 12 the leading '1' of the month '10' is written as a faint tick right at the left margin, so the cell can look like '0-15-16'; escalated to 900 dpi with the crop extended to the page edge, where the tick is visible on lines 10 and 12 and faint on line 11. '0' is not a month, and the run 10-14 / 10-15 / 10-20 / 10-22 is consecutive, so the month is 10; date confidence held at medium for that reason.

AMOUNT REVERSED BY ARITHMETIC: read '152.00' at 200 dpi, which left the page exactly 5.00 short of the cover's 6,333.06; escalated to 1200 dpi, where the third glyph is a flat-topped 7 with a diagonal, giving 157.00 and closing the page to the cent. See line 10's note on the month tick.
